key_insight: A quantics tensor-train (QTT) Chebyshev–Galerkin method solves nonperiodic boundary-value problems directly in compressed form while preserving their variational structure.
engineering_relevance: The method enables accurate elasticity analysis across large design and uncertainty spaces without storing every field coefficient explicitly.
method: Assemble global Chebyshev–Galerkin systems from the weak formulation directly in QTT form.
Handle variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet–Robin conditions.
Treat design parameters and random inputs as extra coordinates for a single joint solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports errors below 10⁻⁸ on a 3D elasticity benchmark, 1.7×10⁷ cantilever designs solved in 92 seconds, and 2.4×10⁶-fold coefficient-storage savings for a ten-random-coordinate problem.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on tensor compressibility; the reported gains may not carry over to problems requiring high tensor ranks.
paper_title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
